about: The prompt-line audition's cases (tests/line_audition.py). Each case is the words a person types after `? ` and what makes an answer right, never one fixed string: head_any (the acceptable head commands, any stage), must_not (regexes the command or answer must not match: a pattern of the text, such as an option or a path), not_head (commands that must not run: each a regex held whole against every head word the command would run, a wrapper such as sudo included, so a path like /var/service or a word inside a quoted pattern is no hit; in an answer in words it is looked for as a word; a hit reports under the rule must_not), must (regexes the command or answer must all match: what a right answer cannot leave out), danger (true, false, or null for either), kind (cmd, answer, or null for either), answer_any (an answer in words must match one), spark_verb (a spark core case: the verbs that answer it; the words are checked against the tree), then (the follow-up of a `??` pair), split (held: a held-out case), why_review (why a review changed the case). The spark cases held-01 to held-24 are held out, frozen on 2026-10-04: never reword one, drop one or add to them, and never tune the prompt or the knowledge on their answers. `run --split dev` leaves them out and the report prints their score on a line of its own; a held question that turns out wrong stays, and a better one goes among the other cases under a new id. oses holds what a run needs to speak as each OS, and what a snapshot job installs first. A spark case with split "more" is a second phrasing added in v1.87 to tune on: reported on its own line, never part of the first report's 34.
